name: Liu Chung-yung
bio: Liu Chung-yung was a T'ang poet of the eighth and ninth centuries. His poem here is a four-line piece on a soldier's long guard on the frontier.
The poem here is Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu's versions in The Jade Mountain (1929), given with the poet's name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: A Trooper's Burden
poems.author: Liu Chung-yung
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
For years, to guard the Jade Pass and the River of Gold,
With our hands on our horse-whips and our sword-hilts,
We have watched the green graves change to snow
And the Yellow Stream ring the Black Mountain forever.

poems.title: 徵人怨 (Zheng ren yuan)
poems.author: Liu Chung-yung
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 七言絕句. Also titled 徵怨.
poems.text:
歲歲金河復玉關，朝朝馬策與刀環。
三春白雪歸青冢，萬里黃河繞黑山。
